newsitem.title: ALBANIA: More foreign troops reach Albanian port of Durres.
newsitem.headline: More foreign troops reach Albanian port of Durres.

text.p: More than one thousand French, Italian and Greek troops on an eight-nation security mission to volatile Albania arrived in the western port of Durres on Friday.

The troops, who brought hundreds of armoured personnel carriers and tanks, raised to more than 2,500 the number of soldiers that have arrived in Albania since the start of Operation Alba (Dawn) earlier this week.

The soldiers are securing humanitarian aid supplies to the violence-stricken nation. Some 300 people have been killed and 700 injured during the weeks of armed anarchy and banditry that swept Europe's poorest country.
"I could cry to see so many tanks, trucks and soldiers in my country," said a 39-year-old Albanian woman named Sabrie, who watched the troops march into Durres. "I know they are going to help us."

Some 530 French troops and 100 vehicles, about 400 Italian troops, 130 Greek soldiers and 34 vehicles landed at Durres. Some 6,000 troops on the U.N.-backed mission are due within the next three weeks.
"The troops are preparing the necessary logistics in different sites," said Lieutenant Colonel Gianfranco Scalas of the Italian army.
Scalas said another 1,000 Italian troops were expected to land at Durres on Saturday.
About 530 French troops and one hundred vehicles reached Durres earlier on Friday.

The Greeks are heading for the southern port of Vlore, where the armed unrest ignited at the end of February. They will stay in Fier, 35 km (20 miles) north of Vlore, for several days, Greek commander Costas Katsikoyianis said.
Only a small force of 25 Italian marines has arrived by land in rebel-held Vlore so far. They were the first troops to reach the south.

The Italian-led multinational force's first task was to secure the three key ports of entry into Albania -- Durres, Vlore and Tirana airport. Durres and Tirana airport were secured on Tuesday, the first day of the mission.

The mission is to prepare the way for the arrival of badly needed aid to the impoverished country, which has been racked by violence and lawlessness since the collapse of fraudulent investment schemes earlier this year.
